title: The First Quarter: Waking
meter: Prose (the Upaniṣad mantras have no meter)
meterNote: The mantras of the Māṇḍūkya Upaniṣad are prose, not verse, so there is no meter to scan. Their rhythm comes from the chant. Notice how this mantra uses pāda and mātrā, the same two words the meter scanner is built on.
translation: The first quarter is Vaiśvānara: its field is the waking state; its awareness turns outward; it has seven limbs and nineteen mouths; and it enjoys the gross world.
translation_hi: पहला पाद वैश्वानर है: उसका क्षेत्र जाग्रत अवस्था है, उसकी चेतना बाहर की ओर है, उसके सात अंग और उन्नीस मुख हैं, और वह स्थूल जगत का भोग करता है।

words.note: eka-ūna-viṃśati 'one less than twenty'. Hindi उन्नीस comes from this.
From √bhuj, as bhoktā in Nirvāṇa Ṣaṭkam.

grammar: Subtractive numbers: एकोनविंशति = 'twenty minus one' = 19, exactly like Latin undeviginti. Hindi उन्नीस, उनतीस, उनचास keep this pattern.
The nineteen mouths (Śaṅkara's commentary): 5 senses + 5 organs of action + 5 vital airs + mind, intellect, ego and citta. Compare the lists in Nirvāṇa Ṣaṭkam.
Science link: waking awareness shows on an EEG as fast beta waves, about 13 to 30 Hz.
